title: crypto2dev_hash_algo_name infers hash type from digest length: fragile for future algorithms
description:
What is awkward: crypto2dev_hash_algo_name() maps digest length (32/48/64) to a hash name string for ECDSA sign/verify. SHA-256, SHA-384, and SHA-512 are today uniquely identified by their output lengths in the 32/48/64 byte range. But the inference is not semantically correct: other algorithms (SHA3-256=32, SHA3-384=48, SHA3-512=64, SHAKE-256=variable) produce the same output lengths.

For ECDSA with TLS this is fine today — ECDSA over P-256 uses SHA-256, P-384 uses SHA-384, P-521 uses SHA-512, all with fixed digest sizes. But the function is not obviously constrained to these cases.

Suggested rewrite: The ECDSA sign info struct (info->pk.eccsign) carries the digest and its length; the hash type is already known by the caller and could be passed explicitly. Alternatively, rename the function to crypto2dev_ecdsa_hash_name_from_len() and add a comment making the assumption explicit: 'Only valid for ECDSA P-256/384/521 with SHA-256/384/512.'
